paragraphs: Diffusion generation involves solving differential equations, and reducing the number of solver steps can compromise sample quality. The paper analyzes two sources of difficulty: deterministic ODE solvers accumulate gradient errors that their trajectories cannot eliminate, while stochastic SDE solvers can amplify errors introduced by taking discrete steps when only a small step budget is available.

AdaSDE addresses this trade-off with a single-step SDE solver that learns one coefficient for each sampling step. Estimated through lightweight distillation, the coefficient adjusts the strength of error correction as generation proceeds. This makes the correction adaptive rather than fixed throughout sampling. The framework can also be combined with existing solvers, extending its usefulness beyond a standalone sampling procedure.

The experiments report state-of-the-art results with five function evaluations: FID scores of 4.18 on CIFAR-10, 8.05 on FFHQ, and 6.96 on LSUN Bedroom. These findings support the paper’s central proposal that adapting stochastic correction can improve the balance between computational cost and generated sample quality.
neurips-2025-adaptive-stochastic-coeffic.tldr: AdaSDE learns a per-step coefficient that adapts stochastic error correction to improve diffusion sampling with few function evaluations.

paragraphs: A text-to-image model can acquire broad knowledge during pretraining yet still need refinement to produce aesthetically strong images that match instructions. Supervised fine-tuning helps, but its value depends heavily on the examples selected. Public datasets often concentrate on particular styles, while general-purpose collections can be expensive to curate and difficult to assess for actual training impact.

The paper proposes using a pretrained generative model to estimate which examples are likely to be especially useful for fine-tuning. Applying this selection method produces Alchemist, a public dataset containing 3,350 samples. The contribution combines a way to identify promising training material with a compact dataset intended for broad use across text-to-image models.

Experiments on five public models show substantial improvements in generation quality while preserving diversity and style. This suggests that carefully chosen examples can provide effective refinement without requiring a large fine-tuning collection. Releasing both the dataset and the resulting model weights also makes the reported approach available for further research.
neurips-2025-alchemist-turning-public-te.tldr: Alchemist uses a pretrained generative model to select 3,350 fine-tuning examples that improve five public text-to-image models.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning agents can make effective decisions while remaining difficult to explain. This creates a practical obstacle when understanding an agent’s behavior matters, particularly in safety-critical applications. The paper builds on Shapley values, a framework from cooperative game theory for assigning contributions, as a principled basis for explanations. Its central concern is the computational expense of producing those explanations.

FastSVERL makes this approach more scalable by approximating Shapley values. Its design explicitly addresses the sequential nature of reinforcement learning: decisions occur within trajectories, and dependencies extend across multiple steps. An explanation method therefore needs to account for behavior unfolding over time rather than treating every decision as an unrelated event.

The method also accommodates off-policy data and is designed to adapt in real time as agent behavior evolves. Together, these capabilities target explanations that remain useful during ongoing learning and changing behavior. The stated contribution is a practical approach to scalable, principled interpretability; the abstract presents these capabilities without attaching numerical performance claims.
neurips-2025-approximating-shapley-expla.tldr: FastSVERL approximates Shapley values to make reinforcement learning explanations scalable across trajectories, off-policy data, and evolving behavior.

paragraphs: State space models efficiently process long sequences, but their recurrence structure can restrict which symbolic patterns they represent. The paper identifies time-invariant, real-valued recurrence as an important source of these limitations. Its Adaptive Unitary State Space Model, or AUSSM, instead uses input-dependent, skew-symmetric recurrence to produce unitary state evolution and increase expressive power.

Using algebraic automata theory, the authors prove that AUSSM can count modulo a number and simulate solvable group automata at finite precision. These results establish access to a broad class of regular languages beyond the capabilities of other SSM architectures considered in the work. They give a formal explanation for why changing the recurrence can improve symbolic sequence processing.

Adaptive recurrence also creates practical efficiency challenges. The authors address them with a separable convolution formulation and CUDA implementation for parallel training. AUSSM and a hybrid interleaved with Mamba outperform prior SSMs on parity and modular arithmetic tasks, while achieving competent long time-series classification performance. The findings connect stronger formal capabilities with a scalable implementation.
neurips-2025-bridging-expressivity-and-s.tldr: AUSSM combines adaptive unitary recurrence with parallel training to expand state space models’ symbolic capabilities and support long-sequence tasks.

paragraphs: Live task guidance requires more than producing a useful set of instructions. An assistant must watch execution, recognize when a step succeeds, and alert the user when a mistake occurs. These responses must arrive at the relevant moment. The paper therefore treats live coaching as an asynchronous video understanding problem, beyond the usual pattern of waiting for a user’s next message.

The authors introduce Qualcomm Interactive Cooking, a dataset and benchmark built on CaptainCook4D. It includes task execution with user mistakes and supplies dense annotations for timed instructions and feedback. Mistake alerts are tied precisely to when the corresponding error becomes visible, making the timing of assistance part of what models must handle.

The work evaluates state-of-the-art multimodal language models and introduces LiveMamba, a streaming model designed for interactive instructional guidance. Its contribution is both a dedicated evaluation setting and a strong baseline for live coaching. Together, these establish a concrete way to study whether an assistant can connect instructions, observed actions, and timely corrective feedback.
neurips-2025-can-multi-modal-llms-provid.tldr: The paper introduces a timed cooking-guidance benchmark and LiveMamba to study assistants that react to task progress and mistakes in live video.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation needs labels at the pixel level, making annotation costly when budgets are extremely small. This paper studies how to choose the pixels whose labels will be most useful. It uses a pretrained diffusion model to obtain representations at multiple scales, capturing both broad image structure and local detail before deciding what to annotate.

Selection proceeds in two stages. First, MaxHerding chooses a small representative pixel subset from each image, followed by refinement into a diverse pool across images. Second, an entropy-augmented disagreement score examines noisy diffusion features at multiple scales. This score incorporates uncertainty about the model’s predictions alongside prediction confidence to identify informative annotation candidates.

Separating diversity from uncertainty gives each stage a distinct purpose: cover varied visual content, then prioritize useful labels within that coverage. Across CamVid, ADE-Bed, Cityscapes, and Pascal-Context, the method significantly outperforms existing baselines under extreme pixel budgets. These results support the stated finding that high segmentation accuracy can be achieved while labeling only a tiny fraction of pixels.
neurips-2025-diffusion-driven-two-stage-.tldr: A two-stage pipeline uses diffusion features to select diverse, informative pixels for segmentation under extremely small annotation budgets.

paragraphs: Sparse rewards make learning difficult because agents receive little feedback while exploring and must connect eventual success to much earlier decisions. The authors argue that complex tasks call for simpler learning goals that are relevant to the target. Exploring tasks without that direction can become intractable in large spaces with long sequences of actions.

DISCOVER builds an automated curriculum by selecting exploratory goals that lead toward the target task. The paper finds that existing reinforcement learning algorithms already contain a useful directional signal, so this selection does not require prior information. The resulting approach aims to make intermediate practice contribute to a particular objective instead of merely expanding the collection of achievable tasks.

The authors connect the method to principled exploration in bandits and bound the time until the target becomes achievable. That bound depends on initial distance to the target but not the volume of the entire task space. In high-dimensional simulations, DISCOVER solves exploration problems that prior state-of-the-art methods could not solve in the reported evaluation.
neurips-2025-discover-automated-curricul.tldr: DISCOVER selects intermediate goals directed toward a target, enabling sparse-reward agents to solve difficult exploration problems in high-dimensional simulations.

paragraphs: Generating several portrait video shots introduces a coordination problem: the person should remain recognizable while appearance, motion, and shot content follow different instructions. EchoShot addresses this within a foundation video diffusion model. Its goal is a native multi-shot generation framework that supports both identity consistency and detailed control over the content of individual shots.

The architecture introduces shot-aware positional embeddings into a video diffusion transformer. These embeddings help represent differences between shots and connect each shot’s visual content to its textual description. The design supports direct training on multi-shot videos without additional computational overhead. The authors also construct PortraitGala, a human-centered video dataset with consistent identities across shots and detailed captions covering faces, clothing, and movement.

Extensions support personalization from a reference image and long-video synthesis with an unbounded shot count. Evaluations report superior identity consistency and attribute-level controllability. The paper presents EchoShot as a promising foundation for broader multi-shot video modeling, while its demonstrated emphasis remains portrait generation.
neurips-2025-echoshot-multi-shot-portrai.tldr: EchoShot uses shot-aware embeddings and multi-shot training data to generate portrait videos with consistent identities and controllable attributes.

paragraphs: Graph foundation models must handle datasets with different features and connection patterns. Mixture-of-experts architectures address this variety by routing each graph to a suitable expert. In an experimental study, however, the authors find that experts ranked second and third by the router outperform the first-ranked expert. This motivates looking beyond the router’s top choice for useful knowledge.

Combining several experts’ outputs can exploit that knowledge but adds substantial computation. Merging their parameters is more efficient, yet a standard merge can deliver suboptimal results. The paper develops two enhanced merging strategies. One takes inspiration from knowledge distillation, aligning the behavior of the merged expert with an ensemble. The other uses parameter similarity to approximate ensemble outputs while preserving diversity.

Both strategies aim to retain the computational advantages of merging while approaching the effectiveness of evaluating multiple experts. Extensive experiments show improved model performance. The findings identify a routing weakness in the studied model and demonstrate practical ways to incorporate knowledge distributed across experts.
neurips-2025-enhanced-expert-merging-for.tldr: Two enhanced expert-merging strategies improve graph foundation models while retaining merging’s computational efficiency.

paragraphs: A learned representation may be reused by several downstream prediction systems, making fairness a concern beyond any one final model. This paper formalizes learning representations with high-confidence fairness guarantees. Its target is to keep demographic disparity in every downstream prediction within a user-selected threshold, while also allowing control over the probability with which that bound holds.

The proposed FRG framework uses an optimized adversarial model to provide these guarantees. The key distinction is that fairness is expressed through an explicit tolerance and a controllable confidence level. This gives the representation-learning problem a concrete statistical target rather than relying solely on whether a particular downstream evaluation happens to show small disparities.

The authors evaluate FRG on three real-world datasets against six state-of-the-art fair representation methods. They report that it consistently bounds unfairness across a range of downstream models and tasks. These experiments support the usefulness of the framework across the tested settings, complementing its formal focus on probabilistic control of demographic disparity.
neurips-2025-fair-representation-learnin.tldr: FRG learns representations with demographic-disparity bounds governed by a user-defined tolerance and a controllable high confidence level.

paragraphs: The paper investigates how hallucinations emerge inside pretrained transformers when input uncertainty is experimentally controlled. It uses sparse autoencoders to examine internal representations of semantic concepts. This provides a way to connect changes in input structure with changes in the model’s internal activity and, ultimately, with unsupported content in its output.

The experiments find that increasingly unstructured inputs activate a growing number of semantic concepts. Under greater uncertainty, models become prone to activating coherent features that are insensitive to the input. Even pure noise reliably triggers a variety of meaningful concepts. Targeted steering confirms that these concepts remain functionally active, linking the observed representations to the model’s processing.

The authors also find that concept patterns within transformer layers can reliably predict output hallucinations in their experiments. This suggests a basis for measuring hallucination risk using internal activity. The contribution is a mechanistic account grounded in controlled uncertainty experiments, with stated implications for alignment, safety, and possible adversarial attacks.
neurips-2025-from-noise-to-narrative-tra.tldr: Controlled experiments link transformer hallucinations to coherent internal concepts that become less sensitive to increasingly unstructured inputs.

paragraphs: Arithmetic circuit design depends on both the choice of components and the connections between them. Existing learning-based optimization methods largely focus on coarse architectural decisions, leaving interconnections to simplified proxies or heuristics. The paper argues that this separation can miss better circuit topologies and introduces Arith-DAS to optimize those connections more directly.

Arith-DAS represents an arithmetic circuit as a directed acyclic graph with multiple relationship types. It formulates interconnect optimization as differentiable edge prediction, allowing fine-grained search over connections without the proxy models identified as a weakness of prior approaches. This brings a previously simplified design stage into the learning-based optimization process.

Experiments on multipliers and multiply-accumulate units show improvements over state-of-the-art learning-to-optimize and conventional methods. The reported gain reaches 27.05% in the hypervolume of the area-delay Pareto front, measuring the quality of available area-versus-delay trade-offs. Integrating optimized units into large AI accelerators yields up to 6.59% delay reduction, showing benefits beyond isolated arithmetic components.
neurips-2025-high-performance-arithmetic.tldr: Arith-DAS optimizes arithmetic-circuit interconnections through differentiable graph edge prediction, improving area-delay trade-offs and accelerator delay in experiments.

paragraphs: Graph transformers use global attention to learn from graph structure, but its quadratic cost makes large graphs difficult to handle. The paper argues that even designs intended to scale can retain expensive operations tied to the whole graph. HubGT tackles this bottleneck by separating graph processing from training and simplifying the work performed during learning.

Its representation uses a hierarchy built from hub labels. The hierarchy provides information about global connections while retaining locality, and the authors show it is more informative than plain adjacency. It is also suited to heterophilous graphs, where connected nodes can differ. Dedicated construction and query algorithms make this representation usable for transformer attention.

HubGT’s precomputation scales linearly with edge count, while training scales linearly with node count. Graph-related computations are removed from the training stage, supporting mini-batches and favorable GPU utilization. Experiments on large benchmarks report improved computational efficiency and mini-batch capability alongside top-tier effectiveness on both homophilous and heterophilous graphs.
neurips-2025-hubgt-fast-graph-transforme.tldr: HubGT precomputes a hub-label hierarchy to remove graph processing from training and scale graph transformers efficiently.

paragraphs: Self-supervised learning can learn by reconstructing an original sample from another view or by aligning different views in a learned representation space. Both approaches are widely used, but choosing between them requires understanding what each preserves. This paper derives closed-form solutions to study how the process that generates views, including data augmentation, shapes the representations learned.

The analysis finds that both approaches need a minimum alignment between augmentations and irrelevant features to become asymptotically optimal as the sample size increases. In the studied setting, having more data alone therefore does not remove the importance of how views are constructed. The authors contrast this requirement with supervised learning.

When irrelevant features have large magnitude, joint-embedding methods require strictly weaker alignment than reconstruction methods. This establishes a conditional reason to prefer prediction in latent space: it can achieve optimality under a less demanding relationship between augmentations and irrelevant features. The result clarifies a trade-off between the paradigms and offers theoretical support for joint embedding’s empirical success on challenging datasets.
neurips-2025-jointembedding-vs-reconstru.tldr: The analysis shows that joint embedding needs weaker augmentation alignment than reconstruction when irrelevant features have large magnitude.

paragraphs: The paper asks whether discussing moral dilemmas changes language models’ judgments in a way resembling human group deliberation. It tests six models either reasoning alone or participating in multi-turn discussions in pairs or groups of three. The focus is a utilitarian shift: greater acceptance of harmful norm violations when they benefit a larger number of people.

For personal dilemmas involving direct harm to an individual for others’ benefit, every tested model judged violations more acceptable in the group condition. However, the apparent similarity to human behavior did not imply the same underlying mechanism. Human group effects are associated with greater sensitivity to outcomes, whereas model groups showed varied profiles, including reduced norm sensitivity or increased impartiality.

The strength and circumstances of the shift differed across models. The authors also discuss prompts and group compositions that increase or reduce it. These findings make deliberation structure relevant to multi-agent design: collaboration can alter moral judgments, and understanding the change requires examining more than the final group answer.
neurips-2025-many-llms-are-more-utilitar.tldr: Across six tested models, group discussion increased acceptance of direct harm for collective benefit, with mechanisms and effect sizes varying by model.

paragraphs: Agricultural consultations often begin with incomplete descriptions and images, leaving an expert to determine what information is missing. MIRAGE evaluates this kind of interaction by combining real user queries, expert-written responses, and visual context. It draws on more than 35,000 user-expert interactions and covers over 7,000 biological entities across crop health, pest diagnosis, and crop management.

The benchmark has two components. The single-turn challenge tests entity identification, causal explanations, and actionable recommendations from one query and its images. The multi-turn challenge tests tracking the conversation, pursuing its goals, and deciding how to proceed. Because inputs are underspecified, models must assess whether to answer or actively guide the exchange toward needed information.

The authors evaluate more than 20 open and closed frontier vision-language models with three reasoning language models serving as evaluators. GPT4.1 and GPT4o reach reported accuracies of 44.6% and 40.9%, respectively. These results show substantial difficulty in the benchmark’s expert consultation tasks, including both individual responses and sustained interactions.
neurips-2025-mirage-a-benchmark-for-mult.tldr: MIRAGE tests whether vision-language models can reason, seek missing information, and guide agricultural consultations grounded in real expert interactions.

paragraphs: Continual learning aims to add new capabilities without losing earlier ones, but storing past training data may be infeasible. Model inversion offers synthetic examples for replay by extracting information from a trained model. The paper identifies two problems: examples generated from compressed class outputs can drift away from real data, and full-model inversion can require many expensive optimization steps.

Per-layer Model Inversion, or PMI, uses layer-specific optimization to produce a strong starting point for subsequent full-model inversion. This reduces the iterations needed for convergence. To address distribution drift, the method models class-wise features with Gaussian distributions and preserves distributional information through a contrastive model. Features sampled for inversion support alignment between synthetic and real feature distributions.

Combining these components, the authors demonstrate incremental learning of new classes using generated data derived from pseudo image features and a semantic-aware projection. They report effectiveness and compatibility across multiple continual-learning settings. The approach links faster synthetic-data generation with better preservation of the feature information that replay is meant to retain.
neurips-2025-model-inversion-with-layer-.tldr: Layer-wise inversion and class-feature modeling make synthetic replay more efficient and better aligned for continual learning without stored past data.

paragraphs: Time-series foundation models can forecast new datasets without task-specific training, but adapting them effectively remains a separate challenge. The authors argue that straightforward fine-tuning often underuses their capabilities and can lead to overfitting. Their starting observation is that temporal patterns differ across sampling scales, while these pretrained models already possess capabilities for forecasting at multiple scales.

The paper analyzes fine-tuning from a causal perspective and uses that analysis to motivate explicitly modeling multiple scales during adaptation. It introduces Multiscale Finetuning, or MSFT, for encoder-based time-series foundation models. The framework incorporates scale-aware modeling directly into the fine-tuning process, making temporal scale part of how the model is adapted to its downstream task.

Experiments use three backbones: Moirai, Moment, and Units. Models adapted with MSFT outperform naive fine-tuning, typical parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches, and state-of-the-art deep-learning methods in the reported evaluation. The results support treating multiple temporal scales as a central part of adaptation, with benefits demonstrated across different pretrained encoder architectures.
neurips-2025-multi-scale-finetuning-for-.tldr: MSFT explicitly models multiple temporal scales during fine-tuning, improving forecasting across three encoder-based time-series foundation models.

paragraphs: Predicting a scene’s future involves both how far ahead to look and how detailed the prediction should be. The paper formalizes these as separate dimensions of Multi-Scale Temporal Prediction. It covers general and surgical scenes, where detailed states belong within broader structures, such as surgical steps within phases. A new benchmark provides synchronized annotations across both dimensions.

The proposed IG-MC method combines incremental visual generation with collaborating decision agents. Generation continually updates visual previews as the prediction horizon expands, keeping those previews synchronized with decisions. This component is intended to maintain prediction quality as forecasts reach further into the future and to provide current visual information to the agents.

A second component coordinates generation, initiation, and multi-state assessment agents to trigger and evaluate prediction cycles. Their collaboration balances consistency across the overall scene with accuracy in detailed states. Experiments on general and surgical scenes demonstrate the method’s effectiveness and the stability of its decision-driven collaboration, supporting its use as a generalizable, plug-and-play approach within the evaluated task.
neurips-2025-multi-scale-temporal-predic.tldr: IG-MC combines progressively updated visual previews with collaborating agents to predict scene states at multiple horizons and levels of detail.

paragraphs: Markov chain Monte Carlo usually generates samples sequentially, so producing a longer chain requires more sequential work. Common hardware-oriented approaches run multiple independent chains at once. This paper instead studies parallel computation across the positions of a chain, aiming to accelerate the evaluation of the sequence itself despite dependencies between successive states.

The method represents the entire state sequence as the solution of a fixed-point problem. A parallel form of Newton’s method then solves that problem. The authors show how this approach applies to Gibbs sampling, Metropolis-adjusted Langevin sampling, and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. They also develop two parallel quasi-Newton methods to reduce the memory requirements and runtime of evaluating nonlinear recursions.

In several examples, the approach simulates up to hundreds of thousands of samples using only tens of parallel Newton iterations. Reported speedups exceed an order of magnitude in some cases compared with sequential evaluation. These results demonstrate that chain-length parallelism can be practically useful across multiple sampling examples, beyond parallelizing independent chains.
neurips-2025-parallelizing-mcmc-across-t.tldr: Parallel fixed-point solvers accelerate computation across MCMC chain positions, producing more than tenfold speedups in some reported examples.

paragraphs: EEG datasets vary in recording protocols, devices, and electrode layouts, making it difficult to learn representations that transfer across setups. The paper argues that existing EEG foundation models often restrict pretraining to one configuration and struggle with these variations. REVE is designed to learn from diverse EEG signals while accommodating differences in signal length and electrode arrangement.

Its central architectural addition is a four-dimensional positional encoding that enables processing of arbitrary signal lengths and electrode configurations. REVE is pretrained with a masked autoencoding objective on more than 60,000 hours of recordings from 92 datasets and 25,000 subjects. This combines a flexible input representation with a large and heterogeneous pretraining collection.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on ten downstream EEG tasks, including motor imagery, seizure detection, sleep staging, cognitive load, and emotion recognition. Strong generalization with little or no fine-tuning suggests that the learned representations transfer effectively across the tested tasks. Code, pretrained weights, and tutorials are released to support further EEG research.
neurips-2025-reve-a-foundation-model-for.tldr: REVE combines flexible positional encoding with large-scale EEG pretraining to transfer across recording setups and ten downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Clustering groups similar observations, but the resulting assignments may be difficult to explain. One approach expresses clusters through an axis-aligned decision tree, whose decisions depend on individual features. Earlier work largely optimized the cost of explainability for particular clustering objectives. This paper seeks a general way to build such an explanation for an existing clustering without restricting which clustering it can accept.

SpEx uses spectral graph partitioning as the basis for constructing the explanation tree. It can fit a tree to a supplied clustering that lacks an explanation or operate directly on the dataset. These two modes make the approach useful both for explaining an existing result and for producing an explainable clustering from the outset.

The authors also connect prior algorithms to graph partitioning through a framework that optimizes cuts in two graphs simultaneously. This provides a shared perspective on methods previously associated with different clustering objectives. Experiments across a range of datasets show favorable performance against baselines, supporting the practical value of the general formulation.
neurips-2025-spex-a-spectral-approach-to.tldr: SpEx uses spectral graph partitioning to fit an interpretable decision tree to any given clustering or directly to a dataset.

paragraphs: Gradient clipping is widely used in centralized and federated learning, but its theoretical analysis often assumes Gaussian noise and standard smoothness. This paper studies weaker conditions: heavy-tailed noise and a generalized smoothness condition called (L0, L1)-smoothness. It seeks convergence guarantees that hold with high probability, providing control beyond statements about performance averaged over randomness.

For clipped stochastic gradient descent, the analysis establishes a better convergence rate than existing results and does not require bounded gradients. The authors then examine federated learning, where simply applying clipped SGD does not close the gap between expected and high-probability convergence. They introduce Federated Clipped Batched Gradient, or FedCBG, to address that problem.

The paper proves high-probability convergence and generalization bounds for the proposed federated algorithm and exposes trade-offs between optimization and generalization. Experiments report better generalization to unseen client distributions than state-of-the-art baselines. Together, the results connect weaker noise and smoothness assumptions with guarantees and empirical behavior relevant to heterogeneous federated data.
neurips-2025-tight-high-probability-boun.tldr: The paper strengthens high-probability guarantees for clipped SGD under weaker assumptions and introduces FedCBG for federated optimization and generalization.

paragraphs: Tubular structures pose a representation challenge because both their detailed shape and their connectivity matter. Voxel and point-cloud representations can require substantial storage while losing fine geometric or topological information. This paper proposes a continuous representation based on Ball B-Spline Curves, together with a network designed to learn from these tubular manifolds.

The framework, SE(3)-BBSCformerGCN, includes a formal definition and analysis of the manifolds and their function space. Its mapping is equivariant to rotations and translations, so changes in pose produce corresponding changes in the representation. The authors also establish geometric and topological stability. Their formulation reduces data complexity while retaining geometric attributes and structural connectivity.

Evaluation focuses on classifying branches of the Circle of Willis using TopCoW 2024 and a clinical dataset. The method consistently outperforms voxel and point-cloud baselines in classification, generalization, convergence speed, and resistance to overfitting. These findings support the value of a continuous, topology-aware representation for the tested vascular shape-analysis task.
neurips-2025-topology-aware-learning-of-.tldr: A rotation- and translation-equivariant network learns continuous tubular representations that improve vascular branch classification while reducing data complexity.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised medical segmentation often learns consistency by perturbing internal features. Many methods use dropout, whose rate can be sensitive and difficult to tune. VQ-Seg introduces a different perturbation mechanism: it first converts features into discrete codebook entries through vector quantization, then modifies their spatial arrangement to provide controllable regularization.

Its Quantized Perturbation Module shuffles the locations of codebook indices. Because quantization can discard information, the architecture shares the resulting feature space between image reconstruction and segmentation branches. A separate Post-VQ Feature Adapter adds guidance from a foundation model to supplement high-level semantic information lost during quantization. These components address both how to perturb representations and how to preserve useful content.

The authors also collect 828 CT scans annotated for central-type lung carcinoma. Experiments on this lung cancer dataset and public benchmarks show that VQ-Seg outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. The findings support discrete token perturbation as an effective alternative to dropout-based consistency learning in the evaluated medical segmentation settings.
neurips-2025-vq-seg-vector-quantized-tok.tldr: VQ-Seg replaces dropout perturbations with shuffled quantized tokens and uses reconstruction and foundation-model guidance to support medical segmentation.
